content: Fluoride is prescribed to prevent tooth decay. It is absorbed by the teeth, where it strengthens them, enhances their resistance to acid, and inhibits the cavity-forming activity of bacteria. This medication is typically recommended for children and adults who live in areas where the water supply is not fluoridated. In some cases, fluoride may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Fluoride is available in liquid form, tablets, and chewable tablets, all of which are taken orally. It is usually taken once daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take fluoride exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. The liquid form can be taken directly from the bottle or mixed with cereal, fruit juice, or other foods. Use a dropper or oral syringe to measure your dose accurately. Tablets can be dissolved in the mouth, chewed, or added to drinking water or fruit juice. They can also be added to water for use in infant formulas or other foods. While fluoride helps strengthen teeth and prevent cavities, it is not a substitute for brushing or flossing. Before taking fluoride, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to fluoride, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and medications), or any other drugs. Additionally, let them know about all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially vitamins. Do not take calcium, magnesium, or iron supplements while using fluoride without consulting your doctor. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking fluoride, contact your doctor. Also, let your doctor know if you are on a low-sodium or sodium-free diet. Avoid consuming dairy products for one hour before or after taking fluoride. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Fluoride may cause side effects. If you experience severe or persistent symptoms, inform your doctor. Minor side effects may include staining of the teeth. Severe side effects requiring immediate medical attention include an unusual increase in saliva, a salty or soapy taste, stomach pain, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, weakness, tremors, or seizures. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store fluoride in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
